report.source_text: Renal biopsy findings revealed nine crescent formations and eight scleroses in 17 glomeruli. Endocapillary hypercellularity was also present. Inflammatory cells had infiltrated into the interstitium. Mild tubular atrophy with interstitial fibrosis was observed by light microscopy. In the mesangium, immunofluorescence assays revealed 2+ diffuse fine granular staining for IgA and 1+ staining for IgM and C3. Electron microscopy revealed dense deposits in the mesangial area (Figure 1A, B).

report.source_text: Two days after the renal biopsy was performed, serum creatinine levels increased from 3.9 mg/dL to 4.8 mg/dL. The patient was treated with prednisolone pulse therapy (250 mg twice daily) for 3 consecutive days; the dose was tapered to 1 mg/kg/day (Figure 2). Planned intravenous cyclophosphamide therapy was canceled because the patient developed abdominal symptoms on the fifth day of steroid treatment. He had watery diarrhea 10 times daily, and laboratory data revealed that he suffered from metabolic acidosis caused by severe diarrhea. Blood gas analysis showed the following parameters: pH 7.24, PaCO2 22.4, PaO2 82.6, and HCO3 9.7. His serum chloride level was 121 mmol/L; BUN and serum creatinine levels were 89 and 3.88 mg/dL, respectively. The patient was treated with 5-ASA (2 g/day) and loperamide (6 mg/day). In addition, intravenous fluid therapy was administered to restore volume loss. The watery diarrhea subsided in 2 weeks, and the patient was discharged.

clinician.trajectory_summary: An 18-year-old male with a history of Crohn's disease presented with azotemia, proteinuria, microscopic hematuria, facial puffiness, and lower extremity edema. His renal function had deteriorated, and he had hypertension. A kidney biopsy revealed rapidly progressive IgA nephropathy, characterized by nine crescent formations and eight scleroses in 17 glomeruli, endocapillary hypercellularity, interstitial inflammation, tubular atrophy, and interstitial fibrosis. Immunofluorescence showed 2+ diffuse fine granular IgA and 1+ IgM and C3 in the mesangium, and electron microscopy showed dense deposits in the mesangial area. Serum creatinine initially increased post-biopsy. He was treated with prednisolone pulse therapy, but planned intravenous cyclophosphamide was canceled due to severe diarrhea and metabolic acidosis. He was subsequently treated with oral deflazacort and cyclophosphamide. Cyclophosphamide was later replaced by azathioprine, and then by mycophenolate sodium due to bone marrow suppression. By December 2011, his renal function had improved (BUN 33.8 mg/dL, creatinine 2.32 mg/dL), and intestinal symptoms were not aggravated.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with acute kidney injury, proteinuria, microscopic hematuria, and edema in the context of Crohn's disease.

Kidney biopsy showed nine crescent formations and eight scleroses in 17 glomeruli, endocapillary hypercellularity, interstitial inflammation, tubular atrophy, and interstitial fibrosis, consistent with rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis.
Immunofluorescence revealed 2+ diffuse fine granular IgA and 1+ IgM and C3 in the mesangium, supporting IgA nephropathy.
Electron microscopy showed dense deposits in the mesangial area, characteristic of IgA nephropathy.
Initial rapid deterioration of renal function (creatinine increase from 3.9 to 4.8 mg/dL post-biopsy) supported the 'rapidly progressive' nature.
Treatment included corticosteroids (prednisolone, deflazacort) and immunosuppressants (cyclophosphamide, azathioprine, mycophenolate sodium).
Renal function improved over several months of treatment (creatinine decreased from 3.88 mg/dL post-diarrhea to 2.32 mg/dL by December 2011).

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Kidney biopsy findings with specific IgA deposition and crescent formation definitively diagnosed IgA nephropathy.

remaining_uncertainties: Long-term renal function trajectory beyond December 2011
